<header class="page-hero about-hero">
<p class="eyebrow">Experience & approach</p>
<h1>I work between the biology and the decision.</h1>
<p>My background covers antibody immunotherapies, precision oncology, developmental neurobiology and building computational tools. The job has been the same in all of them: take a vague question, pull evidence from whatever modalities are available, and say plainly what the data supports and what it does not.</p>
</header>

<section class="about-intro" aria-labelledby="profile-title">
<figure>
<div class="about-photo" role="img" aria-label="Portrait of Rafael Soler Ortuño"></div>
</figure>
<div>
<p class="section-index">Profile</p>
<h2 id="profile-title">Computational biologist with 6+ years across industry and academia.</h2>
<p>I have a PhD in bioinformatics and two years of postdoctoral work in immuno-oncology and tumour biology, using single-cell and spatial transcriptomics, multi-omic integration and machine learning for biomarker discovery, validation and patient stratification. In industry that has meant antibody immunotherapies against TNFR2 and FcγRIIB, mode-of-action studies, and translational work in oncology and autoimmune disease.</p>
<p>The useful part is that I know the biology and can also write the code. I can pick up a question at experimental design and QC and carry it through integration, modelling and interpretation to something an experimental or clinical team can use. The pipelines are R and Python, they run on HPC and AWS, and they are meant to be rerun by someone who is not me.</p>
<p>I have worked in Spain, Germany, the United Kingdom and Sweden, and I am comfortable presenting to people whose background is nothing like mine.</p>

<p class="section-index">Career</p>
<h2 id="career-title">Professional experience</h2>

<div class="experience-list">
<article class="experience-entry">
<div class="experience-meta"><span>Aug 2025 – Aug 2026</span><span>Lund, Sweden</span></div>
<div class="experience-content">
<p class="company">BioInvent International AB</p>
<h3>Bioinformatics Research Scientist</h3>
<ul>
<li>Carried out multi-omic analysis across the BI-1206 anti-FcγRIIB and BI-1808 anti-TNFR2 antibody programmes, integrating scRNA-seq, CITE-seq, spatial transcriptomics, bulk RNA-seq, proteomics and clinical metadata, and connecting evidence across patient, mouse and in-vitro samples to advance mode-of-action and resistance-mechanism understanding.</li>
<li>Uncovered a non-canonical myeloid activation pathway underlying antibody response by resolving distinct immune activation states across a 30-patient clinical PBMC cohort spanning the BI-1808 and BI-1910 programs, extending the mode-of-action pipeline to integrate clinical single-cell RNA-seq with targeted pathway-level analysis.</li>
<li>Characterised drug mechanism of action using scRNA-seq, spatial transcriptomics and targeted gene-module scoring, resolving antibody-responsive immune cell states, macrophage polarisation profiles and tissue niches in blood and tumour microenvironments to support early patient selection.</li>
<li>Validated cell-type-specific genetic regulation of a candidate autoimmune target using a public single-cell eQTL atlas, auditing raw alignment quality and dataset chemistry to protect quantification against multi-mapping read loss within a polymorphic gene family, directly informing a target-validation go/no-go decision.</li>
<li>Established a novel biomarker and therapeutic target for autoimmune disease by curating and integrating public single-cell atlases across three published inflammatory bowel disease cohorts (ulcerative colitis, Crohn's disease and healthy controls), demonstrating specificity restricted to M1 macrophages, inflammatory monocytes and neutrophils.</li>
<li>Strengthened the biological rationale for a novel bispecific target by integrating clinical single-cell and spatial transcriptomics into the biomarker strategy, identifying a significant expression correlation with a canonical regulatory T-cell marker ahead of experimental validation.</li>
<li>Built and trained a variational autoencoder to separate strain-level technical variability from tumour biomarker signal across genetically diverse mouse strains, designed to extrapolate candidate biomarkers to human population heterogeneity.</li>
<li>Delivered a reusable single-cell and spatial immune atlas alongside an AWS-based, Docker-containerised HPC environment built from scratch, enabling reproducible computing across the team, with documented R/Python pipelines, automated QC and reporting for technical and non-technical audiences.</li>
</ul>
</div>
</article>

<article class="experience-entry">

<div class="experience-content">
<p class="company">Bristol Myers Squibb</p>
<h3>Visiting Scientist, Computational Biology</h3>
<ul>
<li>Designed gene signatures from patient tumour samples across lung, pancreatic and breast cancers, applying SNV and mutation analysis to inform precision-medicine and drug-resistance strategies.</li>
<li>Mapped preclinical models (cell lines, xenografts and organoids) to clinical tumour subtypes using TCGA and DepMap/Celligner, improving the translational validity of preclinical findings.</li>
<li>Performed spatial transcriptomics analysis with NanoString CosMx and 10x Visium HD to resolve tissue-level expression programs across tumour cohorts.</li>
</ul>

<article class="experience-entry">
<div class="experience-meta"><span>Sep 2020 – Sep 2024</span><span>Alicante, Spain</span></div>
<div class="experience-content">
<p class="company">Institute of Neurosciences, CSIC–UMH</p>
<h3>Bioinformatics Research Scientist · PhD</h3>
<ul>
<li>Built automated Python, R, Bash and AWK pipelines to integrate RNA-seq and ATAC-seq across phylogenetically distant species, resolving conserved and species-specific genes and enhancers governing cortical development.</li>
<li>Integrated scRNA-seq with RNA-seq and ATAC-seq to define conserved cortical stem-cell types and their gene-regulatory programs across species.</li>
<li>Identified tumour gene signatures in paediatric brain tumours through meta-analysis of public GEO and EGA datasets, benchmarking findings against mouse scRNA-seq, ATAC-seq and bulk RNA-seq models.</li>
<li>Applied deep learning to protein sequence data to predict candidate transcription-factor sequences from structural features, scaling automated workflows across large public datasets.</li>
<li>Built and published an interactive R Shiny single-cell atlas for non-programmer researchers, broadening public access to cortical single-cell data, and mentored two MSc students.</li>
</ul>
